full_judgment: 10. The broad facts of the case are not in dispute. These are, that Delta Jute Mills was established in the year 1963 by securing UK credits in kind in the form of machineries, processed through the IDBP. The promoters agreement was drawn in 1963 providing that the borrower would issue debentures in Rupee currency against the said loan, but later on the parties mutually agreed that the land, building and machineries of the mills would be mortgaged with IDBP instead of rupee debenture. Accordingly, the petitioner-company entered into two credit agreements with the IDBP on 20.7.70 in respect of its loan. After the liberation of the country, the company was nationalised but the same was denationalized on 30.1.83. After the de-nationalised a dispute, however, arose between the petitioner-company and the IDBP in respect of the outstanding liability of the petitioner-company which culminated in the institution of a suit being Title Suit No. 12 of 1986 in the Commercial Court No. 2 Dhaka against Respondent No. 2 and others including Respondent No. 4 seeking a decree for Tk. 2,87,45,611.83 with compensation on declaration that Respondent No. 2 has no claim against it upon allegation that there was an over-payment of the said amount to Respondent No. 2 during the period the company was nationalised and that during pendency of the said suit Respondent No. 2 having issued notice for winding up of the petitioner company for its failure to pay their claim, the petitioner company made an application for temporary injunction restraining Respondent No. 2 from taking any step for its winding up and the court thereupon passed an order on 28.6.86 directing issue of notice upon the said respondent to show cause why temporary injunction, as prayed for, should not be granted against it and the court was further pleased to direct the parties to maintain status quo till the hearing of the injunction matter.
